target_customer: Hospitals, neurosurgeons and psychiatry clinics buying surgical navigation and robotic TMS systems
problem: Image-guided neurosurgery relies on large, costly capital equipment tied to the operating room. Zeta aims to give accurate frameless navigation at many points of care, including bedside procedures and TMS targeting.
business_model: Medical device sales of navigation and robotic systems plus instruments and accessories
product_category: Surgical navigation and medical robotics (AI and computer vision)

founders.name: Jose Maria Amich
founders.background_notes: YC lists him as founder and CEO; no further background found in the sources read.

founders.name: Raahil Sha
founders.background_notes: Experience in computational biology per YC page. A 2021 press release says the company was founded by Harvard graduates and faculty.

technical_complexity.rationale: A small team had to build real-time frameless tracking, registration accuracy suitable for brain procedures, and a regulated Class II device cleared through FDA 510(k), which took years.

defensibility.rationale: FDA clearances (several between 2023 and 2026) and clinical validation are slow to replicate, but incumbent navigation vendors hold large installed bases.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source read shows incumbents copying or buying Zeta. Sources describe those firms as market incumbents in navigation; Zeta remained independent through 2026.

market_need_then: Traditional neuronavigation uses large capital equipment and 2D screens, and procedures such as external ventricular drain placement are often done without guidance. Source for the capital equipment point is a market description, not a 2019 article.

identity.logo: Uppercase wordmark with red and white accents per the company site
identity.visual_style: Clinical medtech, uppercase headings, red and white accent
identity.voice_and_tone: Technical and confident: PRECISION BEYOND THE OR, Unlock the future of surgery

rebrands.why: not stated in sources; a search snippet says the company was formerly Z Imaging and the YC directory has a z-imaging URL

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand itself, no community. Coverage is about FDA clearances and funding. Typical low-profile medtech brand.

outcome_analysis: Zeta Surgical is still operating in 2026 and has built a regulatory position: FDA clearances for its navigation system in 2023 and 2024, navigated instruments in May 2026 and a robotic TMS system in July 2026, plus a first TMS deployment. Funding disclosed in sources is a $5.2M seed in March 2022, so later growth capital is unclear. The slow, regulated path and incumbents in navigation are the main risks.
notes: Funding cross-check: TechCrunch headline says a $5.75M raise while the press release says $5.2M seed; TechCrunch also mentions a $250,000 pre-seed with YC and Plug and Play, recorded here only as a note because no date was seen. Aggregators (CB Insights, VCBacked, Dealroom) show later rounds and totals of $5.0M to $8.5M that could not be verified, so they are not recorded as rounds. Competitor search found nothing dated near 2019 that names Zeta, so the list is empty. Some profiles list a different YC batch; the YC page says Summer 2019. Name origin not found.
